reasons: No test covers this file in the material provided.
Unresolved ids and missing URLs are reported in text instead of failing, so bad data can reach the deck quietly.
Page-order dependence makes link targets fragile when claim order changes.

terms.meaning: the back section of a deck that holds supporting detail, here the source list.
a clickable link inside a slide that jumps to another slide or opens a web page.

a slide type built from fixed rules rather than free layout.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports used by citations
sections.what: Brings in the presentation type, the recipe and citation types, and the shared fonts, width, margin and colour settings used for the appendix.
sections.why: Keeps the appendix looking the same as the rest of the deck.
sections.watch_out: Renaming any setting in the branding file breaks this file.

sections.name: citationKey
sections.title: Building a key for shared sources
sections.what: Builds a text key from a claim's fact ids and project ids, so claims that rely on the same sources share one reference list.
sections.why: Stated in the comment: identical source sets share one bibliography, while source-free gaps and methodology stay separate.
sections.watch_out: The key decides which claims are grouped. If the fact or project ids change, reference lists may split or merge unexpectedly.

sections.name: safeSourceUrl, Row
sections.title: Checking that a web link is safe
sections.what: Accepts a source address only if it is a normal web address (http or https). Otherwise it returns nothing, so the reference row shows no link.
sections.why: Likely reason: stops malformed or unsafe addresses from being written into the deck.
sections.watch_out: Missing or bad URLs are dropped silently, and the row then appears as a citation gap.

sections.name: CitationAppendix (part 1)
sections.title: Collecting sources for each claim
sections.what: Turns each claim's facts and projects into reference rows. Several facts from the same project document are merged into one row, and each claim gets a link to its reference slide.
sections.why: Stated in the comment: internal links work offline, external links open the publisher, and no references are capped.
sections.watch_out: Page numbers are assigned in the order claims are first linked, so reordering claims moves all the link targets.

sections.name: CitationAppendix: render
sections.title: Drawing the reference slides
sections.what: Creates the reference slides, splits long lists across pages, adds previous and next links, a back link to the first citing slide, and speaker notes holding the full recorded text.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps every source visible and reachable without a cap.
sections.watch_out: Nothing is drawn when every slide is a canonical page, because those already carry their own citations.

summary: Builds the citation appendix, the set of slides that list the sources behind each claim and link back to the claims.
purpose: Lets a reader of the deck check where each number or statement came from, offline if needed, and open the publisher page when a link is recorded.
why: Reason not stated in the code, beyond the comment that internal links work offline and external links open the publisher and that no references are capped.
how: First, a key is built for each claim's set of sources so identical sets share one reference list. Next, each claim gets a link to its reference slide, and the reference rows are collected from stored facts and projects. Source links are checked to be normal web addresses. Then the render step draws the reference slides, splitting long lists across pages with previous and next links, a back link to the first citing slide, and full recorded text in speaker notes.
inputs: A recipe result with its facts, projects and slides, and per-claim citation records that list fact ids, project ids, a kind and an explanation.
outputs: Link targets for each claim, and extra appendix slides added to the presentation with their speaker notes. Nothing is added when every slide is a canonical page.
risks: Facts with a missing URL appear as citation gaps rather than failing. Page numbers depend on the order in which claims are first linked, so a change in that order moves every link target. Unknown fact ids are shown as missing evidence records.
debug: If a claim link jumps to the wrong slide, check the order of claim calls in CitationAppendix link and the page count in pageCount. If a source row is missing a link, check safeSourceUrl and the stored URL on the fact. If the appendix does not appear, check whether every slide is marked canonicalPage, since render then returns early.
